findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: read_guide, list_tracks, check_tracks, find_row_email, suggest_hack, test_hack, save_hack, read_inbox, hack_versions, rerun_inbox, add_rows, send_message, dismiss_inbox, get_webhook_link, gmail_forwarding, report_community_hack, find_hacks, rate_template, send_feedback, set_rules · Private data: list_ready_made, get_webhook_link, use_starter, publish_schema · Public sink: read_guide, create_custom_track, list_tracks, find_row_email, suggest_hack, save_hack, add_rows, send_message, get_glance, set_glance, set_questions, get_webhook_link, gmail_forwarding, stop_gmail_forwarding, add_column, get_schema, publish_schema, share_form, find_hacks, share_hack, find_templates, install_template, connect_sheet, share_template, rate_template, send_feedback, set_rules · Destructive: find_row_email, reminders, dismiss_inbox, use_drafted_fix, quick_adds, format_sheet, use_starter, get_schema, update_hack_from_community, set_rules.

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
